The `singlet` package gives you programmatic access to the Singlet
single-cell genomics atlas. You work with two simple things: **GEO
accessions** (such as `"GSE138867"` or `"GSM4120733"`) and **cell searches**
across the whole atlas. Each study is published as one `.s1` object per sample
plus a manifest; the package fetches only the parts it needs, caches them, and
assembles them into the single-cell objects you already use.

The chunks below need network access and download real studies, so they are
not run when the vignette is built. Every one of them works as written
against the public atlas.

## Install

```{r install}
install.packages(c("remotes", "BiocManager"))
BiocManager::install(c("SingleCellExperiment", "SummarizedExperiment", "S4Vectors"))
remotes::install_github("Singlet-Bio/singlet", subdir = "r")
# once on CRAN: install.packages("singlet")
```

```{r setup}
library(singlet)
```

`load()`, `find()`, `find_load()` and `download()` are also available as
`singlet_load()`, `singlet_find()`, `singlet_find_load()` and
`singlet_download()`. The short names mask `base::load()` and
`utils::find()` once the package is attached, so this vignette uses the
`singlet_` names.

## Load a study by accession

Pass a GEO Series accession to `singlet_load()`. The study's manifest and the
parts of its sample objects that hold the count matrices are fetched from
`https://data.singlet.bio`, cached locally, and assembled into a
`SingleCellExperiment`.

```{r load-one}
sce <- singlet_load("GSE138867")
sce
table(sce$gsm_id)
```

Subsequent calls reuse the cached objects instead of downloading them again. The
cache lives in `tools::R_user_dir("singlet", "cache")` by default; override
it with the `cache_dir` argument or the `SINGLET_CACHE_DIR` environment
variable.

## Load a single sample

A GEO Sample accession works too. `singlet_load()` looks up the study it
belongs to, fetches that sample from the study, and keeps only the sample's cells.

```{r load-gsm}
sce <- singlet_load("GSM4120733")
unique(sce$gsm_id)
```

## Per-cell labels

Per-sample studies carry per-cell labels, cell calls and QC columns, and `colData` has them in front of the GEO sample
metadata (`?singlet_labels`):

```{r labels}
sce <- singlet_load("GSE286650")
table(sce$cell_type, sce$sex_chrom)          # CL label at level <= 2 (compartment, lineage)
head(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)[, c("cell_type_ontology_term_id", "cell_type_deepest", "ancestry_hancestro", "called_ed")])
# select cells by label before the matrices are downloaded
cm <- singlet_cells("GSE286650", cell_type == "cardiac muscle cell" & sex_chrom == "male")
```

- `cell_type` / `cell_type_ontology_term_id`: per-study accuracy 0.84 at level 1 and 0.75 at level 2;
  `cell_type_deepest*` holds the deeper call (0.43 / 0.32 at levels 3 / 4, a preview); `cell_type_level = 6L` puts it
  in `cell_type`.
- `sex_chrom`: chromosomal sex, 98.1% agreement with GEO sample metadata. `ancestry_hancestro`: continental HANCESTRO
  category, human donors with coverage tables only.
- `called` is the default cell call and `called_ed` the EmptyDrops call.
- Research Alpha withholds per-cell mitochondrial DNA and doublet columns from every published object.
- The curated GEO fields are `geo_tissue`, `geo_cell_type`, `geo_disease`, `geo_sex` and `geo_age`.

## Combine several studies

Give `singlet_load()` a vector of accessions (or local manifest paths, or a
mix) and it returns one combined object aligned on the shared gene axis.

```{r load-many}
sce <- singlet_load(c("GSE138867", "GSE146974"))
table(sce$gsm_id)
```

Samples with no usable cells (for example an empty count matrix left by a
failed pipeline run) are skipped with a warning instead of failing the load.
The metadata records which ones and why:

```{r skipped}
S4Vectors::metadata(sce)$skipped_samples
```

## Search with natural language

`singlet_find()` turns a free-text description into matching accessions.

```{r find}
hits <- singlet_find("T cells from pediatric AML")
hits

# One accession per sample instead of per study
singlet_find("human PBMC from smokers", level = "gsm", limit = 10)

# Search and load in a single step
sce <- singlet_find_load("microglia from Alzheimer's brain", limit = 5)
```

## Convert to Seurat

Ask for a `Seurat` object directly with `as = "seurat"` (this needs
`install.packages("Seurat")`).

```{r seurat}
obj <- singlet_load("GSE138867", as = "seurat")
obj

# Per-sample metadata is carried into the object's cell metadata
head(obj[[]])
```

## Search the whole atlas for cells

`singlet_search_cells()` counts and locates cells by their labels (cell type,
chromosomal sex, genetic ancestry) and by their sample's metadata (tissue,
disease, stage, organism, assay, ...); ontology terms match their descendants.
`singlet_fetch_cells()` then loads just those cells.

```{r cells}
hits <- singlet_search_cells(list(cell_type = "T cell", sex = "female", tissue = "blood"))
hits
hits$unmapped   # samples a sample-level filter cannot see (no value recorded)

sce <- singlet_fetch_cells(list(cell_type = "B cell", organism = "Homo sapiens", tissue = "blood"),
                           max_cells = 2000)
singlet_cell_fields()   # every field and its coverage
```

## Other modalities

Beyond gene counts, a study's samples can carry spliced and unspliced layers,
splice junctions and PSI and V(D)J usage. Ask what a study has, then load it.

```{r modalities}
singlet_study_modalities("GSE128639")
sce <- singlet_load("GSE128639", modalities = c("counts", "spliced", "unspliced"))
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(sce)
```

## Working offline

`singlet_download()` copies a study's manifest and sample objects into the
cache and returns the local manifest path, which `singlet_load()` reads
without the network.

```{r local}
path <- singlet_download("GSE138867")
sce <- singlet_load(path)
```

## Where the data comes from

Each cell carries its source sample in `colData(sce)$gsm_id`, alongside
tissue, cell type, disease, protocol, and other study metadata when
available. The study's manifest revision and modalities are attached to
`metadata(sce)` for full provenance.

```{r provenance}
SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)
names(S4Vectors::metadata(sce))
```
